## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `status()` line shortens the revision to 7 characters. `history()` and `completed()` use 12, and the docstring says `status()` uses the same identifier as history. As a result, the running status can't be matched by eye to the history output. Apart from that, the change is small and has no error-handling paths.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — `short_revision = revision[:7]` turns `REVISION = "0123456789abcdef..."` into `Running: 0123456 (attempt 2)`, but `history()` at app/display.py:5 prints `History: 0123456789ab`. The docstring at app/display.py:13 says "using the same identifier as history", which contradicts this. The added test at tests/test_display.py:14-15 only checks the prefix and suffix, so it can't catch the mismatch. Could you change this to `revision[:12]` and assert the full string, e.g. `status(REVISION, 2) == "Running: 0123456789ab (attempt 2)"`? — Users who compare a running deployment with history or completion output see two different identifiers for the same revision. A 7-character prefix is also more likely to be ambiguous than the 12-character form used everywhere else.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `attempt_label` is a separate helper, and tests/test_display.py:18-22 checks its exact output for more than one attempt value.

(none)
